title: Apply the meaning filter
summary: When several words fit the grammar, use word pairs, feeling and the meaning of the sentence to choose.

sections.title: Same grammar, different meaning
content: Read: ‘The soup was ___.’ Hot, delicious and enormous are all adjectives, so grammar does not choose for you.
If the next sentence says ‘Everyone asked for more’, delicious is the best choice. Meaning finishes the work that grammar starts.

sections.title: Three meaning checks
content: Word partners: some words naturally go together. We say heavy rain and make a decision, not strong rain or do a decision.
Feeling: words can be positive or negative. Thin and slim describe similar things, but slim sounds positive and thin may not.
Story sense: the word must agree with the events before and after the gap.

sections.title: Work through an example
content: Take: ‘The crowd gave a ___ cheer when the team scored.’ Loud, sad and narrow are all adjectives. A goal makes people happy, so sad does not fit, and cheers are not narrow. Loud is the natural partner.
Take: ‘He took a deep ___ before he spoke.’ Breath and sleep are both nouns. Deep breath is the usual partner, and speaking soon afterwards rules out sleep.

sections.title: Check the partner words
content: At each gap, look for the words around it that the missing word goes with. Say the whole phrase quietly to yourself.

sections.title: Use all three checks
content: These banks have words of the same kind, so grammar alone will not decide. Use word partners, feeling and story sense, and read the whole text again.

sections.title: Find where it went wrong
content: Partner error: the word fits the meaning but is not what English usually says. Feeling error: the word was too positive or too negative. Story error: the word disagrees with what happens next.
Note new word partners in your notebook with the whole phrase.

sections.title: Try a new story
content: Complete one unseen story with eight gaps. You will see your feedback only after you answer every gap. If you need more practice, you will get a new story.
